title: 第五章 过去中的在场

outline.title: 迪士尼乐园里的奴隶制

children: They came long before Columbus. For reasons we can only guess, they had stopped in this arid land where their sole sources of water were gigantic sinkholes nature had carved into the limestone. Here, in the province of Chichén, they had built their temples between two of these wells. They had surveyed the skies from these heights, master astronomers, aware of mathematical secrets that Europeans barely guessed. They were practiced warriors. Most strikingly, they were devout. They had kept one well for themselves and given to their gods the deep one with the green waters.
他们远在哥伦布之前就来了。出于我们只能猜测的原因，他们停在这片干旱的土地上，这里唯一的水源是大自然在石灰岩中凿出的巨大落水洞。在这里，在奇琴（Chichén）地区，他们在两口井之间建起了神庙。他们从这些高处观测天空，是天文学大师，通晓欧洲人几乎无从猜想的数学奥秘。他们是训练有素的战士。最引人注目的是，他们虔诚信神。他们把一口井留给自己，把那口深邃、泛着绿光的井献给了他们的神。

I knew all these stories. I had done my homework before coming to Maya land. Now, I wanted something real. Hunting, my eyes descended the limestone walls eighty feet down into the well. This was the Cenote of Sacrifice, the Sacred Well of Chichén Itzá.
这些故事我都知道。来玛雅人的土地之前，我做过功课。现在，我想要一点真实的东西。我搜寻着，目光顺着石灰岩壁向下八十英尺，落进井里。这就是献祭溶井（Cenote of Sacrifice），奇琴伊察（Chichén Itzá）的圣井。

The still green waters did not speak of war and murder. Not a ripple of blood disturbed their cool surface. Here and there a dead leaf, dropped from the air far above, left a patch of darker green over the underground lake. But there was no movement on the water surface. Here, the past was hidden by a verdant coat of silence.
静止的绿水并不诉说战争与杀戮。没有一丝血的涟漪扰动它清凉的水面。偶尔一片枯叶从极高处飘落，在地下湖上留下一块更深的绿斑。但水面上没有任何动静。在这里，过去被一层苍翠的沉默之衣遮蔽了。

I coughed nervously, sweeping the water with my binoculars. I was in search of evidence. I was eager to see a corpse, a skull, some bones, any gruesome trace of history. But the belly of the earth uttered only the echo of my cough.
我紧张地咳嗽了一声，用双筒望远镜扫视水面。我在寻找证据。我急切想看到一具尸体、一个头骨、几根骨头，任何一点可怕的历史痕迹。但大地的腹中只传出我咳嗽的回声。

Yet history had to be there. Below the water, hundreds of corpses melted into the earth—women, men, and children, many of them thrown alive to deities now forgotten, for reasons now murkier than the bottom of this well. Stories about these sacrifices spanned at least ten centuries. Scavengers of all sorts—colonists, diplomats, warriors, and archaeologists—had unearthed the proofs behind these narratives. Still, I felt disappointed: there was nothing here to touch, nothing to see except a dormant green liquid.
然而历史必定就在那里。水面之下，数百具尸体融入泥土——女人、男人和孩子，其中许多是被活活扔给如今已被遗忘的神祇的，缘由如今比这井底还要晦暗。关于这些献祭的故事至少绵延了十个世纪。各色拾荒者——殖民者、外交官、武士和考古学家——挖出过这些叙述背后的证据。可我还是感到失望：这里没有东西可触，没有东西可看，除了一汪沉睡的绿色液体。

I retraced my steps along the ancient path to the central pyramid. That, at least, seemed concrete, and I had not yet made the journey to the top. Up there, as in the well, history required bodily donations. I had to pay my part of sweat for the encounter to be sincere. Stoically, I climbed the stairs, all 354 of them, and I ventured into the ruins. Inside, for a long time, I ran my fingers on the walls, probing mysteries unresolved, longing for recognition. But as much as I was touched by the magnificence of the structure, I never came to feel that I was touching history. I climbed down the pyramid, careful not to look into the void, blaming myself for this failure to communicate with a past so magnificently close.
我沿着古道折返，走向中央金字塔。那至少显得具体，而且我还没登顶。在上面，和在井里一样，历史要求身体的奉献。我必须付出自己那份汗水，这场相遇才算真诚。我坚忍地爬上台阶，整整354级，然后钻进遗迹。在里面，我久久地用手指抚过墙壁，探查未解之谜，渴望认出点什么。但尽管我被这座建筑的宏伟打动，我始终未能感到自己触摸到了历史。我爬下金字塔，小心不去看那虚空，责怪自己未能与一个如此辉煌地贴近的过去沟通。

Many exotic lands later, I understood better my trip to Chichén Itzá. History was alive and I had heard its sounds elsewhere. From Rouen to Santa Fe, from Bangkok to Lisbon, I had touched ghosts suddenly real, I had engaged people far remote in time and in space. Distance was no barrier. History did not need to be mine in order to engage me. It just needed to relate to someone, anyone. It could not just be The Past. It had to be someone’s past.
又走过许多异域之后，我才更好地理解了我的奇琴伊察之行。历史是活的，我在别处听到过它的声音。从鲁昂到圣菲，从曼谷到里斯本，我触摸过突然变得真实的幽灵，我与时间上空间上遥不可及的人打过交道。距离不是障碍。历史不必是我的才能打动我。它只需要与某个人相关，任何人。它不能只是“过去”（The Past）。它必须是某个人的过去。

In my first trip to the Yucatan, I had failed to meet the peoples whose past Chichén Itzá was. I could not resuscitate a single mathematician viewing the skies from the Caracol, a single sacrificial victim pushed toward the green waters. And I knew even less then how to relate the Mayas of today to the architects of the pyramids. That, no doubt, was my fault, my lack of imagination, or a shortfall of erudition. At any rate, I had missed a vital connection to the present. I had honored the past, but the past was not history.
在我的第一次尤卡坦（Yucatan）之行中，我没能遇见那些把奇琴伊察当作自己过去的人。我无法让一个从卡拉科尔（Caracol）天文台观测天空的数学家复活，也无法让一个被推向绿水、用作牺牲的人复活。而当时我更不知道如何把今天的玛雅人与金字塔的建造者联系起来。那无疑是我的错，是我缺乏想象力，或学识不足。无论如何，我错过了与当下的一个关键连接。我尊崇了过去，但过去不是历史。

en: Slavery in Disneyland
zh: 迪士尼乐园里的奴隶制

en: The controversies about EuroDisney had not yet faded when the mammoth transnational revealed its plans for Disney’s America, a new amusement park to be built in northern Virginia. Aware that environmental and historical tourism are among the fastest growing branches of that industry, Disney emphasized the historical themes of the park. Afro-American slavery was one of them.
zh: 关于欧洲迪士尼（EuroDisney）的争论还没有平息，这家跨国巨头就公布了它的“迪士尼的美国”（Disney’s America）计划——一座将在弗吉尼亚北部兴建的新主题公园。迪士尼深知环境与历史旅游是该产业增长最快的分支，于是强调公园的历史主题。美洲非洲裔奴隶制就是其中之一。

en: Protests immediately erupted. Black activists accused Disney of turning slavery into a tourist attraction. Others intimated that white corporate types were not qualified to address the subject. Others wondered whether the subject should be addressed at all. Disney’s chief imageer tried to calm the public: activists need not worry, we guarantee the exhibit to be “painful, disturbing and agonizing.”
zh: 抗议立刻爆发。黑人活动人士指责迪士尼把奴隶制变成旅游景点。另一些人暗示，白人公司高管没有资格处理这个题材。还有一些人质疑这个题材是否根本就该被处理。迪士尼主管形象塑造的人试图安抚公众：活动人士不必担心，我们保证展览会“令人痛苦、令人不安、令人煎熬”。

en: William Styron, a popular novelist, author of such best-sellers as
and
, denounced Disney’s plans in the pages of

Styron, whose grandmother owned slaves, asserted that Disney could only “mock a theme as momentous as slavery” because “slavery cannot be represented in exhibits.” Whatever the images displayed and the technical means deployed, the artifacts of cruelty and oppression “would have to be fraudulent” because they would be inherently unable to “define such a stupendous experience.” The moral dilemmas of many whites and especially the suffering of blacks would be missing from the exhibit, not because such experiences could not be displayed, but because their very display would beget a cheap romanticism. Styron concluded: “At Disney’s Virginia park, the slave experience would permit visitors a shudder of horror before they turned away, smug and self-exculpatory, from a world that may be dead but has not really been laid to rest.”
zh: 通俗小说家威廉·斯泰伦（William Styron）——《苏菲的选择》（Sophie’s Choice）和《纳特·特纳的忏悔》（The Confessions of Nat Turner）等畅销书的作者——在
上撰文谴责迪士尼的计划。

斯泰伦的祖母拥有过奴隶，他断言迪士尼只能“嘲弄奴隶制这样一个重大的主题”，因为“奴隶制无法在展览中被表征”。无论展示什么图像、动用何种技术手段，用来呈现残酷与压迫的实物“必然给人虚假的印象”，因为它们天生无法“说清如此骇人的经历”。许多白人的道德困境、尤其是黑人的苦难，将在展览中缺席，不是因为这类经验无法展示，而是因为展示本身就会催生廉价的浪漫主义。斯泰伦总结道：“在迪士尼的弗吉尼亚公园里，奴隶经验会让游客先是一阵恐怖的战栗，然后转身离去，得意而自我开脱，把一个也许已死、却并未真正安息的世界抛在身后。”

en: When I first read these lines, I wished a practicing historian had written them. Then it occurred to me that few historians could have done so. Indeed, my second thought was for another novelist writing about yet a third one.
zh: 我初读这些句子时，真希望它们出自一位执业历史学家之手。随后我想到，几乎没有历史学家能写出这样的文字。的确，我的第二个念头转向了另一位小说家，他写的是第三位小说家。

en: In a story often evoked in debates about authenticity, Jorge Luis Borges imagines that a French novelist of the 1930s produces a novel that is word for word a fragmentary version of
Borges insists: Pierre Ménard did not copy

, nor did he try to be Miguel de Cervantes. He rejected the temptation to mimic both Cervantes’s life and style as too facile. He achieved his feat after many drafts, at the end of which his text was the same as that of Cervantes.
Is that second novel a fake and why? Is it, indeed, a “second” novel? What is the relationship between Ménard’s work and that of Cervantes?
zh: 在一个关于本真性的争论中常被引用的故事里，豪尔赫·路易斯·博尔赫斯（Jorge Luis Borges）设想一位1930年代的法国小说家写出一部小说，逐字逐句是
的一个残篇版本。博尔赫斯强调：皮埃尔·梅纳尔（Pierre Ménard）没有抄袭
，也没有试图成为米格尔·德·塞万提斯。他拒绝了模仿塞万提斯的生活与风格这种过于轻巧的诱惑。他反复起草才完成这个壮举，最终写成的片段与塞万提斯原文一字不差。
这第二部小说是赝品吗，为什么？它果真是一部“第二”小说吗？梅纳尔的作品与塞万提斯的作品是什么关系？

en: Disney dropped its plans for the Virginia park, much less because of the controversy about slavery than in reaction to other kinds of pressure.

Still, the plans for the park can be interpreted as a parody of Borges’s parody. Indeed, read against one another, the respective projects of the transnational and of Borges’s fictitious writer provide a pointed lesson about the fourth moment of historical production, the moment of retrospective significance.
zh: 迪士尼放弃了弗吉尼亚公园的计划，与其说是因为奴隶制之争，不如说是对其他压力的反应。
不过，公园计划仍可以被解读为对博尔赫斯戏仿的戏仿。的确，把这家跨国公司的计划与博尔赫斯笔下虚构作家的计划对照着读，能给历史生产的第四时刻——回溯性意义的时刻——上一堂尖锐的课。

en: Neither in the case of the park nor in that of the book is empirical exactitude a primary issue. Disney could gather all the relevant facts for its planned exhibits, just as the words in Ménard’s final draft were exactly the same as those in Cervantes’s

Indeed, the Disney corporation flaunted its use of historians as paid consultants—proof, as it were, of its high regard for empirical exactitude. The limitless possibility for errors remained but, other things being equal, one could imagine a version of Disney’s America as empirically sound as the average history book. Styron, who wrote a controversial novel about slavery, knows this. He expresses concerns about empirical issues, but his emphasis is elsewhere. Styron even admits, although reluctantly, that Disney could duplicate the mood of the times. Modern imageers have enough means to stage virtual reality. Yet Styron remains indignant, and it is this indignation that helps him stir his way through his previous objections toward a conclusion that follows the tourists until
they turn away.
zh: 无论在公园的案例还是在书本的案例中，经验上的精确都不是首要问题。迪士尼可以为它计划的展览搜集所有相关事实，正如梅纳尔最终稿里的文字与塞万提斯

里的文字完全相同。的确，迪士尼公司炫耀它雇用历史学家作付费顾问——仿佛以此证明它对经验精确的高度重视。出错的可能性依然无穷，但在其他条件相同的情况下，人们可以设想一个经验上与普通历史书一样扎实的“迪士尼的美国”版本。写过一部关于奴隶制的争议小说的斯泰伦明白这一点。他表达了对经验问题的关切，但他的重点在别处。斯泰伦甚至承认——尽管不情愿——迪士尼能够复制那个时代的氛围。现代形象师有足够的手段搬演虚拟现实。然而斯泰伦仍然愤慨，正是这种愤慨帮他拨开先前的层层异议，走向一个一直跟随游客到他们转身
的结论。

en: Deconstruction’s most famous line may be Jacques Derrida’s sentence:

children: il n’y a pas de hors-texte.

en: How literally can we take the claim that there is no life beyond the text? To be sure, we may decide not to get out of the amusement park. We can argue that if Disney’s imageers had produced the virtual reality of slavery, the paying tourist would have been projected in history. It would have mattered little then, if that projection were a short or even short-sighted representation. Similarly, we may tell Borges that the issue of authenticity is irrelevant and that both novels are the same, however awkward this phrasing. Yet if such answers are unsatisfactory, then, we need to get out the text(s) and look for life after Disney. And, I would argue, getting out the text enables us also to get out of the tyranny of the facts. The realization that historical production is itself historical is the only way out of the false dilemmas posed by positivist empiricism and extreme formalism.
zh: 解构主义最有名的一句话，也许是雅克·德里达（Jacques Derrida）的这个句子：

children: il n’y a pas de hors-texte

zh: （文本之外无物存在）。我们能在多大程度上照字面接受“文本之外没有生活”这一主张？诚然，我们可以决定不出主题公园。我们可以论证：如果迪士尼的形象师制造出了奴隶制的虚拟现实，付费游客就会被投射进历史。那时，这种投射即便是一个短暂甚至短视的表征，也几乎无关紧要。同样，我们可以告诉博尔赫斯：本真性问题无关紧要，两部小说就是同一部，尽管这个措辞很别扭。然而，如果这类回答不能令人满意，那么我们就需要走出文本，去寻找迪士尼之后的生活。而且我要论证，走出文本也使我们得以走出事实的暴政。认识到历史生产本身是历史性的，是摆脱实证主义经验论与极端形式主义所设虚假两难的唯一出路。

en: In the subtext of Styron’s objections is a fundamental premise: Disney’s primary public was to be white middle-class Americans. They are the ones for whom the park was planned, if only because their aggregate buying power makes them the prime consumers of such historical displays. They are the ones most likely to have plunged into the fake agony of Disney’s virtual reality. Styron does not spell out this premise, expressed only through innuendos. Perhaps he wants to avoid accusations of bending to “political correctness.” Perhaps he wants to avoid the issue of collective white guilt. He is careful to suggest, quite rightly in my view, that the exhibit would have misrepresented the experiences of both blacks and whites.
zh: 斯泰伦异议的潜台词里有一个根本前提：迪士尼的主要公众将是美国白人中产阶级。公园就是为他们规划的，单是因为他们的总体购买力使他们成为这类历史展示的主要消费者。他们也是最有可能一头扎进迪士尼虚拟现实之虚假煎熬的人。斯泰伦没有明说这个前提，只通过暗示表达。也许他想避免被人指责屈从于“政治正确”。也许他想回避白人集体罪疚的问题。他小心地暗示——在我看来相当正确——展览会同时歪曲黑人和白人的经验。

en: The value of a historical product cannot be debated without taking into account both the context of its production and the context of its consumption.

It may be no accident that this insight comes from a popular novelist in the pages of a mass market daily. At any rate, few academic historians would have set the problem in these terms; for academic historians are trained to neglect the very actor that Styron or
cannot ignore, the public. The nature of that public is at the center of Styron’s objections.
zh: 不兼顾历史产品的生产语境与消费语境，就无法讨论它的价值。
这一洞见出自一位通俗小说家、发表在一份大众市场日报上，也许并非偶然。无论如何，几乎没有学院历史学家会以这样的措辞设定问题；因为学院历史学家所受的训练，恰恰是忽略斯泰伦或
无法忽略的那个行动者——公众。那个公众的性质正是斯泰伦异议的核心。

en: To phrase the argument in these terms is immediately to reintroduce history or, better, to refuse to get out of it for the seraphic comfort of the text or the immutable security of The Past. Styron refuses to separate the history of slavery from that of the United States after the Civil War. He devotes just a few lines to the time after Union cavalry men invaded his grandmother’s plantation, to the fate of the ex-slaves, to Jim Crow laws and the Ku Klux Klan, and to illiteracy among blacks. He adds, almost in passing, that this post-slavery period is what actually haunts him.
zh: 以这样的措辞表述论证，就是立刻重新引入历史，或者更确切地说，是拒绝为了躲进文本的安逸、或“过去”永不变动所带来的安全感而走出历史。斯泰伦拒绝把奴隶制的历史与内战后美国的历史分开。他只用了寥寥数行写联邦骑兵进占他祖母种植园之后的时光，写前奴隶的命运，写吉姆·克劳法与三K党，写黑人中的文盲现象。他几乎是顺带补充说，真正萦绕着他的，正是这个后奴隶制时期。

en: The time that elapsed between the demise of slavery and the planning of the Virginia park shaped the meaning of Disney’s representation of slavery. Time here is not mere chronological continuity. It is the range of disjointed moments, practices, and symbols that thread the historical relations between events and narrative. Borges’s Ménard makes this complex point in simpler terms: “It is not in vain that three hundred years have passed, charged with the most complex happenings—among them, to mention only one, that same

We could parody him further: it is not irrelevant that a century of complex occurrences has passed in the United States, while slavery hangs on as an issue. That U.S. slavery has both officially ended, yet continues in many complex forms—most notably institutionalized racism and the cultural denigration of blackness—makes its representation particularly burdensome in the United States. Slavery here is a ghost, both the past and a living presence; and the problem of historical representation is how to represent that ghost, something that is and yet is not.
zh: 从奴隶制消亡到弗吉尼亚公园规划之间流逝的时间，塑造了迪士尼奴隶制表征的意义。这里的时间不是单纯的年代连续。它是一系列脱节的时刻、实践与符号，把事件与叙述之间的历史关系串联起来。博尔赫斯笔下的梅纳尔用更简单的措辞说明了这个复杂的论点：“三百年没有白过，其间充满了最复杂的事件——只举其一，就是那部
我们可以进一步戏仿他：一个世纪的复杂事变在美国过去，而奴隶制仍作为一个议题悬而未决，这并非无关紧要。美国的奴隶制既已正式终结，却又以许多复杂形式延续——最显著的是制度化的种族主义和对黑人身份的文化贬损——这使得对它的表征在美国格外沉重。奴隶制在这里是一个幽灵，既是过去又是活着的在场；而历史表征的问题，就是如何表征这个幽灵，这个存在而又不存在的东西。

en: I disagree, therefore, with Styron’s comment that the Holocaust Museum in Washington is illuminating and that displays of slavery in Virginia would be obscene because of some inherent difference in magnitude or complexity between the two phenomena described. That argument rests on the assumption of a fixed past. But the cost accounting of historical suffering makes sense only as a presence projected in the past. That presence (“look at me now”) and its projection (“I have suffered”) function together as a new exhibit for claims and gains in a changing present. Many European Jews who condemn projects of parody at Auschwitz or elsewhere in Poland, Germany, France, or the Soviet Union deploy the same moral arguments that Styron uses against mock plantations today in Virginia.
zh: 因此，我不同意斯泰伦的评论：他说华盛顿的大屠杀博物馆有启发意义，而弗吉尼亚的奴隶制展示会流于亵渎，因为所描述的两种现象在规模或复杂性上有某种内在差异。这个论证建立在一个固定的过去的假定之上。但对历史苦难的成本核算，只有作为一种被投射进过去的在场才有意义。那个在场（“看看现在的我”）和它的投射（“我受过苦”）共同运作，成了人在变化不定的当下提出诉求、争取权益时拿出来的新展品。许多欧洲犹太人谴责在奥斯维辛、或波兰、德国、法国、苏联别处搞戏仿项目，他们动用的道德论证，与斯泰伦今天用来反对弗吉尼亚模拟种植园的如出一辙。

en: Do displays of Jewish genocide run greater risks of being obscene in Poland than in Virginia? The illuminating value of the Holocaust Museum in Washington may be as much tied to the current situation of American Jews as to the real bodies in and around Auschwitz. Indeed, many Holocaust survivors are not sure that such a museum would be illuminating at Auschwitz itself. The crux of the matter is the here and now, the relations between the events described and their public representation in a specific historical context.
zh: 犹太种族灭绝的展示，在波兰比在弗吉尼亚更容易流于亵渎吗？华盛顿大屠杀博物馆的启发价值，也许既系于奥斯维辛及其周边真实的尸体，也同样系于美国犹太人当前的处境。的确，许多大屠杀幸存者并不确定，这样一座博物馆设在奥斯维辛本地是否就有启发意义。问题的症结在此时此地，在所描述的事件与它们在特定历史语境中的公共表征之间的关系。

en: These relations debunk the myth of The Past as a fixed reality and the related view of knowledge as a fixed content. They also force us to look at the purpose of this knowledge. What is scary about tourist attractions representing slavery in the United States is not so much that the tourists would learn the wrong facts, but rather, that touristic representations of the facts would induce among them the wrong reaction. Obviously, the word “wrong” has different meanings here. It denotes inaccuracy in the first case. In the second, it suggests an immoral or, at least, unauthentic behavior.
zh: 这些关系戳穿了把“过去”当作固定现实的神话，以及与之相关的把知识当作固定内容的看法。它们也迫使我们审视这种知识的目的。在美国，表征奴隶制的旅游景点之所以可怕，与其说在于游客会学到错误的事实，不如说在于对这些事实的旅游式表征会在他们中间诱发错误的反应。显然，“错误”一词在这里有不同的含义。前一种情况指不准确。后一种情况则暗示一种不道德的、或至少不本真的行为。

en: Cascardi suggests that “authenticity is not a type or degree of knowledge, but a relationship to what is known.”

To say that “what is known” must include the present will seem self-evident, but it may be less obvious that historical authenticity resides not in the fidelity to an alleged past but in an honesty vis-à-vis the present as it re-presents that past. When we imagine Disney’s project and visualize a line of white tourists munching on chewing gum and fatty food, purchasing tickets for the “painful, disturbing and agonizing” experience promised by television ads, we are not into The Past. And we should not ask these tourists to be true to that past: they were not responsible for slavery. What is obscene in that image is not a relation to The Past, but the dishonesty of that relation as it would happen in our present. The trivialization of slavery—and of the suffering it caused—inheres in that present, which includes both racism and representations of slavery. Ironically, a visit by a Klan member actively promoting racial inequality would have stood a better chance of authenticity. At least, it would not have trivialized slavery.
zh: 卡斯卡迪（Cascardi）提出：“本真性不是一种知识的类型或程度，而是与所知之物的关系。”

说“所知之物”必须包括当下，似乎不言自明；但也许不那么明显的是：历史的本真性不在于忠实于某个据称的过去，而在于诚实地面对那个重新表征该过去的当下。当我们想象迪士尼的计划，眼前浮现一队白人游客嚼着口香糖、吃着油腻食物，排队购买电视广告许诺的“令人痛苦、令人不安、令人煎熬”的体验门票时，我们并不在“过去”之中。我们也不该要求这些游客忠实于那个过去：他们对奴隶制没有责任。那幅图景中亵渎性的东西，不是与“过去”的关系，而是这种关系在我们的当下发生时的那种不诚实。对奴隶制——及其造成的苦难——的琐碎化，内在于那个当下，而那个当下既包括种族主义，也包括对奴隶制的种种表征。具有讽刺意味的是，一个积极鼓吹种族不平等的三K党成员前来参观，反而更有可能具备本真性。至少，他不会把奴隶制琐碎化。

en: One understands why many practicing historians kept silent. The denunciation of slavery in a presentist mode is easy. Slavery was bad, most of us would agree. But, presentism is by definition anachronistic. To condemn slavery alone is the easy way out, as trivial as Pierre Menard’s first attempt to become Cervantes. What needs to be denounced here to restore authenticity is much less slavery than the racist present within which representations of slavery are produced. The moral incongruence stems from this uneasy overlap of the two sides of historicity.
zh: 人们可以理解为什么许多从事史学研究的历史学家保持沉默。以当下主义的方式谴责奴隶制是容易的。奴隶制是坏的，我们大多数人都会同意。但当下主义按定义就是时代错置的。仅仅谴责奴隶制是一条轻松的出路，就像皮埃尔·梅纳尔最初试图成为塞万提斯一样琐碎。要恢复本真性，这里需要谴责的与其说是奴隶制，不如说是生产奴隶制表征的那个种族主义的当下。道德上的不协调，正源于历史性两侧这种令人不安的重叠。

en: Not surprisingly, survivors of all kinds are more likely than historians to denounce these trivializations. Thus, Vidal-Naquet warns us that if Holocaust narratives, even if empirically correct, lose their relationship to the living present, Jews and perhaps non-Jews would have suffered a moral defeat, and Holocaust survivors would have been returned symbolically to the camps. Pierre Weill approves in different terms: There is no purpose to the speeches and banners that marked the fiftieth celebration of Auschwitz’s liberation by Soviet troops. The celebrations were a vain effort by state officials throughout the West to commemorate an impossible anniversary.
zh: 不出所料，各类幸存者比历史学家更有可能谴责这些琐碎化。于是，维达尔-纳凯（Vidal-Naquet）警告我们：如果大屠杀叙述即便在经验上正确，却失去了与活着的当下的关系，那么犹太人、也许还有非犹太人，就遭受了一场道德失败，而大屠杀幸存者就被象征性地送回了集中营。皮埃尔·韦伊（Pierre Weill）以不同的措辞表示赞同：那些标志着苏军解放奥斯维辛五十周年庆典的演讲与横幅毫无意义。这些庆典是整个西方的国家官员为一场不可能的周年纪念所做的徒劳努力。

en: Survivors carry history on themselves, as Vidal-Naquet well knows. Indeed, a key difference between U.S. slavery and the European Holocaust is that no former slaves are alive today in the United States. This physical embodiment, a historical relation carried on the self, is crucial to Vidal-Naquet’s distinction between history and memory. Thus, Vidal-Naquet worries about representations of the Holocaust once his generation is gone. But we should be careful not to push too far the distinction between various kinds of survivors. Weill, indeed, refuses to do so: As long as every living Jew, “regardless of age,” remains an Auschwitz survivor, one cannot celebrate the liberation of Auschwitz.
zh: 幸存者把历史带在自己身上，维达尔-纳凯深知这一点。的确，美国奴隶制与欧洲大屠杀的一个关键区别在于：今天的美国没有一个前奴隶还活着。这种身体性的体现，这种承载于自身的历史关系，对维达尔-纳凯区分历史与记忆至关重要。因此，维达尔-纳凯担忧他那一代人逝去之后的大屠杀表征。但我们应当小心，不要把各类幸存者之间的区分推得太远。韦伊恰恰拒绝这样做：只要每一个活着的犹太人，“无论年龄大小”，仍是奥斯维辛的幸存者，就不能庆祝奥斯维辛的解放。

en: We are back into this present that we thought we could escape after the death of the last man.

It is from within this present that survivors, actors, and fellow narrators are asking us: what for? The meaning of history is also in its purpose. Empirical exactitude as defined and verified in specific context is necessary to historical production. But empirical exactitude alone is not enough. Historical representations—be they books, commercial exhibits or public commemorations—cannot be conceived only as vehicles for the transmission of knowledge. They must establish some relation to that knowledge. Further, not any relation will do. Authenticity is required, lest the representation becomes a fake, a morally repugnant spectacle.
zh: 我们又回到了这个当下——我们曾以为，在最后一个人死去之后就能逃离它。
正是从这个当下内部，幸存者、行动者和叙述者同伴们在问我们：为了什么？历史的意义也在于它的目的。在特定语境中界定并核实的经验精确，对历史生产是必要的。但仅有经验精确并不够。历史表征——无论是书籍、商业展览还是公共纪念活动——都不能仅仅被设想为传递知识的载体。它们必须与那种知识建立某种关系。而且，并非任何关系都行。必须有本真性，否则表征就成了赝品，成了道德上令人憎恶的景观。

en: By authenticity, I do not mean a mere simulacrum, a remake of Columbus’s caravels, a mock battle on an anniversary or an exact model of a slave plantation. Neither do I mean a plunge into The Past. For how far can we plunge without trying to become Miguel de Cervantes in the way that Ménard first tried and found cheap and too easy? To be sure, injustices made to previous generations should be redressed: they affect the descendants of the victims. But the focus on The Past often diverts us from the present injustices for which previous generations only set the foundations.
zh: 我说的本真性，不是指单纯的拟像，不是重造哥伦布的轻快帆船，不是周年纪念日上的模拟战斗，也不是奴隶种植园的精确模型。我指的也不是扎进“过去”。我们若不想成为米格尔·德·塞万提斯，又能扎进过去多深呢？梅纳尔最初试过成为他，后来觉得这样做廉价而且太容易。诚然，对前几代人施加的不义应当纠正：它们影响着受害者的后代。但聚焦于“过去”，常常使我们偏离当下的不义——前几代人为这些不义奠定的只是基础。

en: From that viewpoint, the collective guilt of some white liberals toward “the slave past” of the United States, or the “colonial past” of Europe can be both misplaced and inauthentic. As a response to current accusations, it is misplaced inasmuch as these individuals are not responsible for the actions of their chosen ancestors. As a self-inflicted wound, it is comfortable inasmuch as it protects
from a racist present.
zh: 从那个观点看，某些白人自由派对美国的“奴隶制过去”或欧洲的“殖民过去”所怀的集体罪疚，既可能错置，也可能不本真。作为对当前指控的回应，它是错置的，因为这些个人对其所选祖先的行为并无责任。作为一道自加的伤口，它又是舒适的，因为它让
可以不必直面当下的种族主义。

en: Indeed, none of us today can be true to Afro-American slavery—whether for or against it—as we can be true to ongoing practices of discrimination. Similarly, individuals in the Old World or in Latin America today cannot be true or false to a colonialism they did not live. What we know about slavery or about colonialism can—should, indeed—increase our ardor in the struggles against discrimination and oppression across racial and national boundaries. But no amount of historical research about the Holocaust and no amount of guilt about Germany’s past can serve as a substitute for marching in the streets against German skinheads today. Fortunately, quite a few prominent German historians understand that much.
zh: 的确，美洲非洲裔奴隶制已是过去，无论赞成还是反对，我们今天都无法像面对仍在持续的歧视那样，用行动表明自己的立场。同样，今天旧世界或拉丁美洲的个人，也无法对他们未曾经历过的殖民主义做到忠实或不忠实。我们对奴隶制或殖民主义的了解，能够——的确应当——增强我们跨越种族与国界、反对歧视与压迫的斗争热情。但再多关于大屠杀的历史研究，再多对德国过去的罪疚感，都不能替代今天走上街头反对德国光头党的游行。幸运的是，相当多知名的德国历史学家明白这一点。

en: Authenticity implies a relation with what is known that duplicates the two sides of historicity: it engages us both as actors and narrators. Thus, authenticity cannot reside in attitudes toward a discrete past kept alive through narratives. Whether it invokes, claims, or rejects The Past, authenticity obtains only in regard to current practices that engage us as witnesses, actors, and commentators—including practices of historical narration. That the foundations of such practices were set by our precursors with the added value of their respective power is an inherent effect of the historicity of the human condition: none of us starts with a clean slate. But the historicity of the human condition also requires that practices of power and domination be renewed. It is that renewal that should concern us most, even if in the name of our pasts. The so-called legacies of past horrors—slavery, colonialism, or the Holocaust—are possible only because of that renewal. And that renewal occurs only in the present. Thus, even in relation to The Past our authenticity resides in the struggles of our present. Only in that present can we be true or false to the past we choose to acknowledge.
zh: 本真性意味着与所知之物的一种关系，这种关系也有历史性的两个面向：它让我们同时作为行动者和叙述者介入。因此，本真性不可能存在于对一个通过叙述而保持鲜活的离散过去的态度之中。无论它援引、认领还是拒绝“过去”，本真性只在与让我们作为见证者、行动者和评论者介入的当前实践的关系中获得——包括历史叙述的实践。这些实践的基础由我们的先行者奠定，并附加了他们各自权力的增值，这是人类境况之历史性的内在效果：我们谁都无法从零开始。但人类境况的历史性也要求权力与支配的实践不断翻新。最应让我们关切的正是这种翻新，即便我们是以各自过去的名义去关切它。所谓过去恐怖的遗产——奴隶制、殖民主义或大屠杀——之所以可能，正是因为这种翻新。而这种翻新只发生在当下。因此，即便在与“过去”的关系中，我们的本真性也存在于我们当下的斗争之中。只有在那个当下，我们才能忠实于或背离我们选择承认的过去。

en: If authenticity belongs to the present, academic historians—and quite a few philosophers—may have lured themselves into a corner. The traditions of the guild, reinforced by a positivist philosophy of history, forbid academic historians to position themselves regarding the present. A fetishism of the facts, premised on an antiquated model of the natural sciences, still dominates history and the other social sciences. It reinforces the view that any conscious positioning should be rejected as ideological. Thus, the historian’s position is officially unmarked: it is that of the nonhistorical observer.
zh: 如果本真性属于当下，那么学院历史学家——还有相当多的哲学家——也许已把自己诱入了死角。行会的传统，在实证主义历史哲学的加持下，禁止学院历史学家就当下表态。一种以过时的自然科学模型为前提的事实拜物教，仍然支配着历史学和其他社会科学。它强化了这样一种看法：任何自觉的立场表态都应作为意识形态而加以拒绝。于是，历史学家的位置在官方上是无标记的：那是非历史观察者的位置。

en: The effects of this stance can be quite ironic. Since historical controversies often revolve on relevance—and therefore, at least in part, on the positioning of the observer—academic historians tend to keep as far away as possible from the historical controversies that most move the public of the day. In the United States, a few have intervened in the historical debates that made news in the early 1990s: the alleged role of Jews as slave owners, the Holocaust, the Alamo, the Smithsonian exhibits on the American West and on Hiroshima, or the Virginia park project.

But many more qualified historians have kept public silence on these and similar issues. That silence even extends to debates about the national standards for history that academics seem to have abandoned to pundits and politicians.
zh: 这种姿态的效果可能相当讽刺。由于历史争论往往围绕某段历史与当下的关联——因而至少部分围绕观察者的立场——展开，学院历史学家倾向于尽可能远离那些最牵动当时公众的历史争论。在美国，少数人介入了1990年代初成为新闻的历史辩论：所谓犹太人作为奴隶主的角色、大屠杀、阿拉莫、史密森学会关于美国西部和广岛的展览，或弗吉尼亚公园计划。
但更多合格的历史学家对这些问题及类似问题保持公开沉默。这种沉默甚至延伸到关于全国历史课程标准的辩论——学者们似乎已把这些标准拱手让给了时事评论员和政客。

en: To be sure, the distance between scholarly and public discourses in the United States is extreme when compared, for instance, with the situation in France or in Germany.

American scholars have largely abandoned the role of public intellectual to pundits and entertainers. But the U.S. extreme tells us something about the continuum to which it belongs. At the heart of the noninvolvement of U.S. historians is the guild’s traditional attachment to the fixity of pastness.
zh: 诚然，与比如法国或德国的情况相比，美国学术话语与公共话语之间的距离是极端的。
美国学者大体上把公共知识分子的角色让给了时事评论员和艺人。不过，美国这个极端例子也有助于看清各国学界参与公共辩论的程度如何不同。美国历史学家不介入的核心，是行会对过去性之固定性的传统依恋。

en: Professional historians have made good use of the creation of the past as a distinct entity, a creation that paralleled the growth of their own practice.

That practice, in turn, reinforced the belief that made it possible. The more historians wrote about past worlds, the more The Past became real as a separate world. But as various crises of our times impinge upon identities thought to be long established or silent, we move closer to the era when professional historians will have to position themselves more clearly within the present, lest politicians, magnates, or ethnic leaders alone write history for them.
zh: 职业历史学家充分利用了把过去创造为一个独立实体的做法，这种创造与他们自身实践的增长并行。
而这种实践反过来又强化了使之为可能的信念。历史学家越是书写过去的世界，“过去”就越是作为一个分离的世界而变得真实。但随着我们时代的种种危机冲击那些被认为早已确立、或一向不被言说的认同，我们正走近这样一个时代：职业历史学家将不得不更明确地在当下之中表态，以免政客、大亨或族群领袖独自替他们书写历史。

en: Such positions need not be fixed, nor should they imply the ideological manipulation of empirical evidence. Practicing historians who advocate a history aware of its purpose—from the presentists of the first half of this century to the leftists of the 1970s—never suggested such manipulation.

Most of these advocates, however, assumed the possibility of either an unambiguous narrative, or of an unambiguous present. With varying degrees of certitude, they envisioned that narratives about the past could expose with utmost clarity positions solidly anchored in the present. We now know that narratives are made of silences, not all of which are deliberate or even perceptible as such within the time of their production. We also know that the present is itself no clearer than the past.
zh: 这类立场不必是固定的，也不应意味着对经验证据的意识形态操纵。主张历史研究应自觉追问其目的的历史学家——从二十世纪上半叶的当下主义者到1970年代的左派——从未主张过这种操纵。
然而，这些倡导者大多假定了一种不含混的叙述或一个不含混的当下是可能的。他们以不同程度的确信设想：关于过去的叙述能够极其清晰地展露牢牢锚定于当下的立场。我们现在知道，叙述是由沉默构成的，并非所有沉默都是刻意的，甚至并非所有沉默在其生产的时代内都能被察觉为沉默。我们也知道，当下本身并不比过去更清晰。

en: None of these discoveries entails an absence of purpose. They certainly do not entail an abandonment of the search and defense of values that distinguish the intellectual from a mere scholar.

Positions need not be eternal in order to justify a legitimate defense. To miss this point is to bypass the historicity of the human condition. Any search for eternity condemns us to the impossible choice between fiction and positivist truth, between nihilism and fundamentalism, which are two sides of the same coin. As we move through the end of the millenium, it will be increasingly tempting to seek salvation by faith alone, now that most deeds seem to have failed.
zh: 这些发现都不意味着目的的缺席。它们当然不意味着放弃对那种把知识分子与单纯学者区分开来的价值的寻求与捍卫。
立场不必永恒，也能为正当的辩护提供理据。看不到这一点，就是绕开了人类境况的历史性。任何对永恒的追求，都迫使我们在无法取舍的选项之间作选择：虚构或实证主义真理、虚无主义或原教旨主义——它们是同一枚硬币的两面。当我们走过千年之交（原文 millenium，当作 millennium），既然大多数行动似乎都已失败，单靠信仰寻求救赎将越来越有诱惑力。

en: But we may want to keep in mind that deeds and words are not as distinguishable as we often presume. History does not belong only to its narrators, professional or amateur. While some of us debate what history is or was, others take it in their own hands.
zh: 但我们不妨记住：行动与言辞并不像我们通常假定的那样可以区分。历史不只属于它的叙述者，无论职业还是业余。当我们中的一些人还在争论历史是什么、曾经是什么时，另一些人已经把历史抓到了自己手里。

en: William Styron, “Slavery’s Pain, Disney’s Gain,”
, 4 August 1994.
zh: William Styron, “Slavery’s Pain, Disney’s Gain,”
, 4 August 1994.

en: Jorge Luis Borges, “Pierre Ménard, Author of Don Quixote,” in

en: Many historians and Civil War buffs had fought the project because they felt that the proposed park would blot out important war sites. Environmentalists, in turn, had raised an uproar about crowding and traffic congestion. In both cases, the loudest objections focused more on the proposed site than on the intrinsic value of the project. In the same tone, Disney’s official announcement was that the company would look for a “less controversial” site. Some analysts saw in the announcement a graceful way for Disney to abandon the project altogether.

1579, 9–15 February 1995, 51. The divergences between Vidal-Naquet’s stance and mine are mostly—but not only—terminological. He calls “memory” a living relation to the past, in part because he believes in a scientific history based implicitly on a nineteenth-century model of science. I explicitly reject that model both for the natural sciences and for the systematic historical investigations performed by professionals. For the record, Weill’s statement should not be dismissed as the individual complaint of a Jew maladjusted within France’s social structure: he is the president of the powerful Sofres group.
